references.text: The Samaritan woman had just left her water jar and gone into the city to tell about Jesus (see John 4:28-29). Verse 30 is the direct result of her testimony: the people went out of the city and came to him.
The result of the Samaritans coming out to Jesus is described in John 4:39-42, where many came to believe – first because of the woman's testimony, then because of Jesus' own words.

Jesus uses the coming Samaritans as a picture of the spiritual harvest that is ripe: "Lift your eyes and look at the fields, they are white for harvest" (John 4:35). The crowd streaming out from the city was itself an illustration of this.

Just as Nathanael came to Jesus after Philip's invitation (John 1:46-47), the Samaritans came to Jesus after the woman's testimony. Both show the pattern that personal testimony leads others to Christ.
In Matthew 8:34, the whole city went out to meet Jesus, but there to ask him to leave. In John 4:30, people went out of the city to come to him – a strong contrast in reception.
Philip's preaching in Samaria (Acts 8:5-8) can be seen as an extension of what began with the Samaritan woman's testimony. The Samaritans showed themselves open to the gospel already here in John 4.
The prophecy in Isaiah 55:5 that nations who did not know God would run to him finds partial fulfillment when the Samaritans – who did not belong to the Jewish people – streamed out to meet Jesus.
